page: Amazon Web Services m6in.16xlarge is a network-optimized general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C). Operating on an x86_64 architecture, it provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores at 3.5 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache. Memory stands at 256 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio.

Network performance is a primary differentiator, delivering a 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance features no bundled local storage, requiring attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent filesystem operations. It includes vector and cryptography instruction sets such as AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI, but does not provide hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate high throughput in parallelized workloads. The instance achieves strong top-quartile results in multi-core metrics, including PassMark CPU (57,720.48), PassMark database operations (26,418.28), and Clang software compilation (41,747.0). Static web serving throughput reaches 44.25 GB/sec. Single-core performance falls in the average median tier, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,700.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,893.89.

Given its 100 Gbps network capacity and balanced compute density, the m6in.16xlarge is architected for network-bound data processing, high-traffic web tiers, clustered relational databases, Redis caching layers, and continuous integration pipelines requiring high inter-node communication bandwidth without local drive storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.16xlarge is a general-purpose, network-enhanced cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processors. Featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs, 32 physical cores, and 256 GB of DDR4 memory, it delivers a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio complemented by a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations, and contains zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation shows upper-quartile execution in multi-core compute, database operations, static web throughput, and large-scale software compilation, while single-threaded tasks perform at the median tier. Hardware cryptography and AVX-512 VNNI support further enhance computational efficiency. This configuration is best matched with network-intensive workloads, including high-traffic application serving, distributed databases, large-scale ETL pipelines, and synchronized multi-node backend systems.
